warning_texts: audit/check_plan.json lists claims_rendered and caveats_rendered for gate_release_document under accepted_unproven, because their plan proof failed with a missing-file error, so that gate's 15 PASS comparisons come from rules never shown to fire; at this stage the only check of rendering and caveats

No deterministic rule at this stage recomputes a release number from source: gate_release_document only tests presence, and gate_release_machine records binding as a summary without a checks.json. The shown numbers agree with the registry here, but their tie to raw_data rests on gate_claims_machine,

The rule that the release generator holds no business-number literals rests only on gate_release_machine's zero issue count; its evidence lists no per-generator scan result, and src/release is not among this auditor's inputs, so nothing independent covered that rule here.

release/report.md line 11 shows the refund-rate numerator and denominator with no unit word; only the caveat line just above says they are paying customers, and it uses the snake_case identifier paying_customers rather than plain words, which is correct but easy to misread.

In metrics/calculated_metrics.json, net_revenue keeps the gross sum (40235.02) in its numerator field with a null denominator; the release does not show that field, but a later reader of the registry could take it for a ratio component.
summary: All 7 numbers a reader sees in release/report.md trace from the page to a claim, then to calculated_metrics, and match exactly. The same 21 bindings across report, dashboard and manifest were found independently and agree with gate_release_machine. The three country figures sum to the headline 35741.52, and the report says so in visible text. 27/57 = 0.4736842105 rounds to the shown 0.473684 on the paying_customers basis. Gross 40235.02 minus refunds 4493.50 = 35741.52. Row accounting holds: 174+26+1 = 201. Every claim's caveats appear in visible text on both surfaces, no HTML comment carries
